title: Traffic recovery and graceful unwind playbook
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working playbook for returning traffic after a controlled experiment or an incident where we want to unwind to a steady-state without causing subsequent spikes or regressions. Focused on model-routing changes, batch-size tuning, and preserved latency SLOs. Use for post-canary unwind, emergency mitigation after a partial degradation, or staged reintroduction after capacity pressure.

Principles (quick):
- Move slowly, observe often: reintroduce traffic in small, time-boxed increments and monitor SLOs for at least two full 95th-percentile windows (30m–2h depending on route).
- Symmetry over speed: prefer symmetric increases across regions to avoid hot spots unless capacity gating requires localized ramps.
- Shadow validation: keep a 5–10% shadow feed to the previous variant for quality regressions for the first 6 hours.
- Bounded rollback: every step must have clear rollback conditions and a pre-authorized rollback owner.

Operator checklist (pre-unwind):
- [ ] Confirm primary runbook lead and secondary for next 24h (name + pager).
- [ ] Post short status message to #release-ops and #sre (template at bottom).
- [ ] Ensure telemetry retention for the next 72h includes traces, token-level costs, and token latency histograms.
- [ ] Reserve a traffic-wallet (capacity hold) equal to 20–30% of expected incremental QPS for 2h windows.
- [ ] Kick off a capacity shadow run: 10m spike of expected per-region QPS while measures are validated in canary lane.
- [ ] Warm KV caches in all serving pools with sample prefixes if applicable.

Unwind tempo (recommended windows):
- Phase 0 — Quiescent baseline (0–30m): keep existing reduced footprint; sanity checks only.
- Phase 1 — Micro-bump (30–90m): +5–10% global traffic, maintain symmetry across regions, 15m observation intervals.
- Phase 2 — Measured ramp (90–240m): +20–35% global, staggered per-region per 30m if capacity varies.
- Phase 3 — Recovery plateau (4–12h): keep at ~70–90% of target, enable shadow validation and slow quality checks.
- Phase 4 — Full return (12–72h): resume 100% if KPIs stable for two plateau windows; otherwise freeze and escalate.

Throttle-symmetry matrix (quick triggers):
- Latency P95 increase > 15% sustained for 2 consecutive windows => pause ramp, reduce to previous step.
- Error rate (500/5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase => immediate rollback to last green variant.
- Token cost per request > 20% variance from baseline => evaluate batching/quantization config before further ramp.

Observability checklist (must be green for each step):
- [ ] P50/P95/P99 latency (route-level) trending stable or improving.
- [ ] Error budget consumption monitored (SLO dashboards).
- [ ] End-to-end trace sampling at 5% (increase to 20% on anomaly).
- [ ] Token throughput and KV cache hit-rate.
- [ ] Cost sketch: per-token unit and per-request delta.
- [ ] Quality signals: sampling of model outputs against fixed prompt-set (10–50 examples every 30m).

Rollback and escalation (owners):
- Immediate rollback owner: on-call release engineer (primary).
- Secondary: serving-runtime on-call.
- Escalation to SRE manager if rollback conditions persist for > 30m after rollback.

Communications templates (short):
- Post to #release-ops (phase transitions):
  "Phase 2 in progress — +30% global traffic. Watching P95 and errors. Primary: Aisha Patel (pager). If errors spike > 0.5%, will rollback to vX.Y within 10m."
- Customer-facing status snippet (for CS template):
  "We are performing a staged traffic reintegration for model routing changes. We expect brief fluctuations in latency as traffic equilibrates; we will update at each phase boundary."

Mini calendar (example next-12h plan — timestamps in UTC):
- 2026-10-12 08:00 — Pre-unwind checks and shadow validation (30m)
- 2026-10-12 08:30 — Phase 1: +10% (observe 15m)
- 2026-10-12 08:45 — Telemetry checkpoint and sample quality run
- 2026-10-12 09:15 — Phase 2: +30% (observe 30m per region)
- 2026-10-12 10:45 — Plateau monitor (4h telemetry sampling cadence)
- 2026-10-12 14:45 — Decision point: continue ramp or freeze
- 2026-10-13 08:00 — Final decision: full return or rollback (72h window complete)

Sample release notes (draft) — short and customer-safe:
Title: Model routing fix and batch-tuning for lower latency
What changed: Adjusted routing weights to prefer v2.3 (quantized) for low-latency paths and tuned batching thresholds for short prompts. Small runtime kernel tweak to lower attention cache eviction frequency.
Why: Reduce 95th percentile latency for chat endpoints by ~8–12% and lower per-token cost for short requests.
Rollout: Staged rollout starting 2026-10-12 UTC. Will ramp in 4 phases with automatic rollback triggers (see internal runbook).
Impact: Expected improvements for most customers; minor risk of temporary latency blips during ramp. No data migration or breaking API changes.
Notes for CS: If customers report output quality drift, collect prompt examples and open ticket RLSE-3124; tag as "quality-sampling".

Quality sampling plan (fast):
- Keep a 10% shadow to v2.2 for first 6h.
- Automated diff run every 30m against canonical prompt-set (20 prompts). Fail if mean BLEU/semantic-similarity delta exceeds threshold X (internal).

Post-mortem anchors (if rollback happens):
- Timeline: capture minute-level decisions and trace IDs for first 120m after ramp started.
- Retrospective checklist: capacity, kernel change review, model quantization validation, routing config change.
- Owners: Aisha (release), Marco (serving), Leah (observability), Diego (CS liaison).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a lightweight run that warms long-sequence KV cache paths prior to Phase 1 if customer mix has >20% long-context usage.
- Formalize the traffic-wallet allocation in the console (console ticket).
- Decide metric thresholds for semantic-similarity (confer with applied-ml).

Draft status: this is a working draft for the next unwind exercise on 2026-10-12. Use and edit liberally; please add precise metric thresholds and confirm on-call rotations prior to scheduling.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (release engineer)
